title: Historic Built Environments
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Facts (to confirm): Stone Town (Zanzibar), Kilwa Kisiwani ruins (Tanzania), Kasubi Tombs (Uganda), rock-hewn churches of Lalibela (Ethiopia), Fort Jesus, Lamu and Gedi (Kenya).

skills.key_step: The child names historic built environments of Eastern Africa and the country of each.

floor.question: Name a historic site in Mombasa.

steps: Say what it was used for.

board.do: Write Lalibela, Stone Town, Kasubi Tombs.

misconceptions.ask: Which one is a historic built environment?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: did people build it or was it made by nature?

misconceptions.ask: In which country are the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela?
misconceptions.repair: Match sites and countries on a small table and say each aloud.

misconceptions.ask: Who built Fort Jesus in Mombasa?
misconceptions.repair: Ask about the date: 1593 is before the British came.

misconceptions.ask: In which country are the Kasubi Tombs?
misconceptions.repair: Put a pin for each site on the regional map.

checks.question: In which country is Stone Town?
Is Mount Kilimanjaro a historic built environment?

skills.key_step: The child explains why historic sites matter and picks ways to conserve them.

floor.prerequisite: Names historic sites of the region.
floor.question: Name a historic site in Ethiopia.

steps: Give one thing it teaches or gives.

board.do: Draw an old wall with a crack.
Wait for careful repair with old materials.
Write two reasons the site matters.

listen_for: They are useless and should be pulled down
misconceptions.ask: Why do we conserve old buildings and museums?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what a visitor learns at Lamu Old Town.

listen_for: Writing your name on the old wall
misconceptions.ask: Which action conserves a historic site?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to a wall when a thousand visitors write on it.

misconceptions.ask: Give a reason a historic site matters besides tourism.
misconceptions.repair: Ask what a learner learns on a visit.

listen_for: Pull it down and build a concrete one
misconceptions.ask: An old coral wall is cracking. Which is the better repair?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a photo of a careful coral repair with a concrete wall.

checks.question: Give two reasons historic sites are important.
checks.answer: any two of: teach history, give identity, bring tourists and income, jobs, research

checks.question: Give one way of conserving a historic site.
checks.answer: any of: careful repair, visitor rules, no writing on walls, guards, teaching others
